desc: Derive the characterization: absorbed set is a contiguous interval with an order-independent closure; final interval is the minimal interval containing K whose two boundaries (if present) are >= the interval sum.
Implement the O(N) max Cartesian tree (leftmost-max tie-break via strict `<` pop), subtree sums T, local "stuck" check, and reach[] climbing DP producing per-node answers.

Verify the reach DP argument: final closure interval equals subtree(m) for the leftmost maximum m; climb requires T[c] > A[parent] (necessary since sum ⊆ subtree(c), and sufficient by induction), and stops exactly at m since A[parent(m)] >= T[m]. Confirmed on multiple hand-worked cases including ties.
Stress-test against a brute-force closure simulator on many random small arrays, emphasizing duplicates and ties; no mismatches. Re-verified both public samples.
